state.task: Our Swift iOS app at `~/repos/trail-buddy` is a hiking companion that uses Siri Shortcuts so users can say "Start my hike" to begin GPS tracking, has a Lock Screen widget showing elevation gain via WidgetKit, and uses Core Haptics to buzz distinct patterns when you reach trail milestones. We also recently added In-App Purchases via StoreKit 2 for premium trail maps and integrated the Photos Picker so hikers can attach photos to trail logs. Before we submit to the App Store next week, I need two things done: first, run a full Qodana code inspection across the entire project — I want to see all the unused imports, any retain cycle risks, force-unwrap issues, dead code from our old StoreKit 1 integration, and any Swift concurrency warnings (we're using async/await heavily in the App Intents handlers and the Siri Shortcut donation logic). Parse out the results grouped by file with severity levels so I can triage. Second, based on whatever Qodana flags in our iOS integration layer, help me fix the issues — particularly I'm worried about our `HikeIntentHandler` that conforms to `AppIntent` for Siri and Spotlight, the `ElevationWidget` timeline provider that might have a data race, the `HapticEngine` singleton that I suspect has a retain cycle with the closure-based pattern callbacks, and the `StoreKit.Transaction.listener` task that might not be getting cancelled properly in `PremiumMapStore`. Also review whether our `PHPickerConfiguration` setup is correctly requesting `.images` only and whether we need to update our `NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription` for the new iOS 17 privacy changes.
